</div><ix:continuation id="_DebtDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_4"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Interest expense related to the Note consists of both (i) contractual
interest at the stated rate and (ii) non-cash interest expense related to the amortization of the debt discount. For the three months
ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized total interest expense of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c115" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:InterestExpenseDebt" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7793">1,673,245</ix:nonFraction>, consisting of contractual interest of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c114" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPaymentInterest" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7794">1,013,699</ix:nonFraction> and
amortization of debt discount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c114" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfDebtDiscountPremium" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7795">659,546</ix:nonFraction>.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 24, 2026, the Company paid $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c116" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:PrincipalPlusAccruedInterestInCashInSatisfaction" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7796">50.0</ix:nonFraction> million principal plus accrued
interest in cash in satisfaction of its obligations under the Note.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Note Payable</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On March 25 2026, in connection with the amendment of certain real
property agreements, the Company, through its subsidiary, agreed to pay total consideration of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c117" decimals="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AgreedToPayTotalConsideration" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7797">4.35</ix:nonFraction> million, consisting
of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c117" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:CashPaid" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7798">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million paid in cash upon execution and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c117" decimals="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:EvidencedByPromissoryNote" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7799">3.35</ix:nonFraction> million evidenced by a promissory note (the &#8220;Note&#8221;).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Note bears interest at a fixed annual rate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c118" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtPercentageBearingFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7800">3.7</ix:nonFraction>%, calculated
on a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c119" format="ixt-sec:durday" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentTerm" id="ixv-7801">360</ix:nonNumeric>-day basis and compounded annually. The Note matures on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c119" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" id="ixv-7802">July 20, 2026</ix:nonNumeric>, at which time all outstanding principal and accrued but
unpaid interest are due and payable in full.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Note is unsecured. As of March 31, 2026, the outstanding principal
balance of the Note was $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c118" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentAnnualPrincipalPayment" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7803">3,347,500</ix:nonFraction>, with accrued interest of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c119" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentIncreaseAccruedInterest" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7804">2,064</ix:nonFraction>.</p></ix:continuation><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On March 31, 2026, the Company issued a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c120" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:OtherLiabilities" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7816">5,000,000</ix:nonFraction> promissory note
to Zachary Zhou who beneficially owns more than <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c121" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7817">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The transaction was reviewed and approved by the
Company&#8217;s Audit Committee and Board of Directors. The note was amended and restated on April 6, 2026.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The amended and restated note bore interest at <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7818">5.00</ix:nonFraction>% per annum, was
subject to a repayment premium equal to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtorInPossessionFinancingInterestRateOnBorrowingsOutstanding" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7819">102</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding principal and accrued interest, and provided for repayment or conversion
upon the occurrence of certain financing events or upon maturity.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 10, 2026, the amended and restated promissory note was fully
converted into <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c122" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockSharesConverted1" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7820">1,522,389</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock in accordance with its terms.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_AssetRetirementObligationDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-3956"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 8. ASSET RETIREMENT OBLIGATIONS</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Company has a number of oil and gas wells in production and will
have AROs that will be settled once the wells are permanently removed from service. The primary obligations involve the removal and disposal
of surface equipment, plugging and abandoning the wells and site restoration.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">AROs associated with the retirement of tangible long-lived assets are
recognized as liabilities with an increase to the carrying amounts of the related long-lived assets in the period incurred. The fair value
of AROs is recognized at the date a new well is completed or the acquisition date of the working interest. The cost of the tangible asset,
including the asset retirement cost, is depleted over the life of the asset. AROs are recorded at estimated fair value, measured by reference
to the expected future cash outflows required to satisfy the retirement obligations discounted at the Company&#8217;s credit-adjusted
risk-free interest rate. Accretion expense is recognized over time as the discounted liabilities are accreted to their expected settlement
value. If estimated future costs of AROs change, an adjustment is recorded to both the ARO and the long-lived asset. Revisions to estimated
AROs can result from changes in retirement cost estimates including revisions to estimated inflation rates, revisions to estimated discount
rates and changes in the estimated timing of abandonment.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

    <td style="border-bottom: Black 4pt double; text-align: left">$</td><td style="border-bottom: Black 4pt double; text-align: right"><ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligation" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7834">12,627,122</ix:nonFraction></td><td style="padding-bottom: 2.5pt; text-align: left">&#160;</td></tr>
  </table></ix:nonNumeric>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During 2025, the Company&#8217;s two helium contracts expired. With
no supporting helium contracts, the Company was unable to justify carrying helium volumes in forecasted Proved Helium reserves. As a result,
the estimated economic lives of many of our producing properties shortened considerably, therefore resulting in a large change in ARO
estimates.</p></ix:continuation><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Amendment to Equity Purchase Facility Agreement</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During 2025, the Company entered into a series of amendments to its
existing Equity Purchase Facility Agreement (EPFA) dated December 6, 2024. These amendments modified certain pricing restrictions and
ultimately increased the Company's right to sell common stock to the Investor from $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c147" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:InvestorsPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7851">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million to $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c148" decimals="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:InvestorsPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7852">1.0</ix:nonFraction> billion. On October 16, 2025,
the Company provided notice to terminate the EPFA, effective October 24, 2025. The Company did not incur any penalties in connection
with the termination.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Warrants &#8211; As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, there
were <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c149" decimals="INF" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7853">5,750,000</ix:nonFraction> Public Warrants and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c150" decimals="INF" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7854">230,750</ix:nonFraction> Private Warrants outstanding. common stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c149" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7856">11.50</ix:nonFraction> per share.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><ix:continuation id="_StockholdersEquityNoteDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Pursuant to a securities purchase agreement, dated December 6, 2024,
by and between us and ATW AI Infrastructure II LLC (the &#8220;Investor&#8221;) (together with the Form of First Tranche Warrant and Form
of Second Tranche Warrant issued on December 6, 2024, the &#8220;Warrant Purchase Agreement&#8221;), we issued and sold to the Investor
warrants to purchase shares of our common stock, comprised of two tranches (the &#8220;First Tranche Warrant&#8221; and &#8220;Second
Tranche Warrant&#8221; and together, the &#8220;Investor Warrants&#8221;). The Warrant Purchase Agreement was amended by that certain
Amended and Restated Consent and Waiver, dated January 16, 2026, by and between us and the Investor (the &#8220;Waiver&#8221;), pursuant
to which, among other things, the Investor agreed to partially waive the anti-dilution provisions of the First Tranche Warrant and Second
Tranche Warrant such that the exercise prices of the First Tranche Warrant and Second Tranche Warrant were each adjusted down solely to
$<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c151" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7857">2.00</ix:nonFraction>. The Investor also waived certain provisions of the Warrant Purchase Agreement relating to restrictions on Variable Rate Transactions
(as defined in the Warrant Purchase Agreement), additional issuances of equity securities, redemption or payment of cash dividends, and
stock splits. The parties agreed to certain administrative updates to the Warrant Purchase Agreement including cashless exercise after
<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" format="ixt-sec:durday" name="nehc:EffectiveDateOfAmendedWaiver" id="ixv-7858">75</ix:nonNumeric> days from the effective date of the Waiver (solely to the extent a resale registration statement is not effective), registration rights
obligations, the provision of a transfer agent instruction letter, and a forced exercise provision granting the Company the right to force
exercise of the Investor Warrants assuming certain conditions are met. The Investor Warrants may be exercised on any day on or after December
6, 2024, in whole or in part at $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c152" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7859">2.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, subject to certain adjustments as provided in the applicable Warrant.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The number of shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the
First Tranche Warrant is equal to the quotient of (i) the product of (x) $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c153" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ClassOfWarrantOrRightDeterminationOfNumberOfSharesIssuableNumerator" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7860">10</ix:nonFraction> million minus any amounts previously paid to exercise the
Investor Warrants and (y) multiplied by <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c153" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ClassOfWarrantOrRightDeterminationOfNumberOfSharesIssuableNumeratorMultiplicationFactor" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7861">110</ix:nonFraction>%, and (ii) divided by the exercise price then in effect. Currently, the number of shares of
common stock issuable upon exercise of the First Tranche Warrant is equal to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c153" decimals="INF" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ClassOfWarrantOrRightIssuable" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7862">5,500,000</ix:nonFraction>, assuming an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c153" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7863">2.00</ix:nonFraction>. The number
of shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the Second Tranche Warrant, assuming an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c154" decimals="INF" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7864">2.00</ix:nonFraction>, is equal to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ClassOfWarrantOrRightIssuable" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7865">10,700,000</ix:nonFraction>.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align: left; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During the period from February through March 2026, the Company received
exercise notices for a portion of the Investor Warrants, resulting in the issuance of an aggregate of approximately <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c155" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7866">5,674,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-4222"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 11. COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Legal Actions</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">From time to time, the Company may be a party to various proceedings
and claims incidental to its business. While many of these matters involve inherent&#160;uncertainty, the Company believes that the amount
of the liability, if any, ultimately incurred with respect to these proceedings and claims will not have a material adverse effect on
the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position as a whole or on its liquidity, capital resources or future annual results of operations.
The Company records reserves for contingencies when information available indicates that a loss is probable, and the amount of the loss
can be reasonably estimated.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Environmental Matters</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left; margin: 0pt 0">The Company, as a lessee of oil and gas properties, is subject to various
federal, provincial, state and local laws and regulations relating to discharge of materials into, and protection of, the environment.
These laws and regulations may, among other things, impose liability on the lessee under an oil and gas lease for the cost of pollution
clean-up resulting from operations and subject the lessee to liability for pollution damages. In some instances, the Company may be directed
to suspend or cease operations in the affected area. There can be no assurance, however, that current regulatory requirements will not
change, or past noncompliance with environmental laws will not be discovered on the Company&#8217;s properties.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Irrevocable Standby Letter of Credit and Promissory Note</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left; margin: 0pt 0">On September 24, 2020, the Company entered into an irrevocable standby
letter of credit (&#8220;LOC&#8221;) and a promissory note with West Texas National Bank in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c158" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7885">25,000</ix:nonFraction> with variable interest
initially of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c159" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityInterestRateDuringPeriod" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7886">4.25</ix:nonFraction>% per annum and maturing on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c159" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" id="ixv-7887">December 24, 2021</ix:nonNumeric>. No amount was drawn down under this LOC up to the date it was amended
on October 29, 2021.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left; margin: 0pt 0">On October 29, 2021, the Company entered into an amendment of the LOC
a new promissory note, increasing the amount to $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c160" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7888">425,000</ix:nonFraction> with variable interest initially of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c161" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityInterestRateDuringPeriod" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7889">4.25</ix:nonFraction>% per annum and maturing on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c161" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" id="ixv-7890">September
29, 2026</ix:nonNumeric>. On January 1, 2022, and March 29, 2022, the LOC was amended, and new promissory notes were executed increasing the amount to
$<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c162" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7891">650,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c163" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7892">920,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. As of March 31, 2026, and December 31, 2025, no amount was drawn down under the LOC.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Limited Liability Company Agreement</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Texas Critical Data Centers (&#8220;TCDC&#8221;) Joint Venture</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On January 21, 2025, the Company and SharonAI formed TCDC, a joint
venture designed to purchase, develop, and operate a Texas-based 250 MW gas-fired power plant and data center. The Company evaluated the
arrangement under ASC 810, <i>Consolidation</i>, and ASC 323, <i>Investments&#8212;Equity Method and Joint Ventures</i>, concluding that
the joint venture should not be consolidated and is appropriately accounted for under the equity method. During 2025, the Company made
total capital contributions to TCDC of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c164" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ContributionJointVenture" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7893">825,000</ix:nonFraction>.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On January 16, 2026, the Company acquired SharonAI&#8217;s equity
interests in TCDC pursuant to the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement, dated as of January 16, 2026, by and between the Company
and SharonAI, for an aggregate purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c165" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AggregatePurchaseAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7894">70</ix:nonFraction> million, of which (a) $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c151" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:Cash" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7895">10</ix:nonFraction> million was payable in cash, (b) $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c165" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireEquitySecuritiesFvNi" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7896">10</ix:nonFraction> million was
payable in equity securities to be issued in connection with the Company&#8217;s next equity financing transaction, and (c) $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c151" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebt" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7897">50</ix:nonFraction>
million was payable in the form of a senior secured convertible promissory note. &#160;Pursuant to the agreement, the number of
shares to be issued in satisfaction of the equity consideration was determined based on the contractual pricing provisions set forth
in the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement. The entirety of the acquisition consideration is subject to a <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c166" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7898">19.99</ix:nonFraction>% ownership cap.
On March 31, 2026, the Company paid SharonAI $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c167" decimals="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:Cash" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7899">9.85</ix:nonFraction> million in cash and issued to SharonAI <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c1" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7900">2,091,351</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock in
satisfaction of the Company&#8217;s obligation to pay $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c168" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ContractualObligation" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7901">10</ix:nonFraction> million in equity securities under the Membership Interest Purchase
Agreement. The number of shares issued resulted in an implied contractual value of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ContractualValuePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7902">4.78</ix:nonFraction> per share. For accounting
purposes, the shares issued were measured at fair value on the issuance date based on the Company&#8217;s closing stock price of
$<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ContractualValueClosingStockPerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7903">4.06</ix:nonFraction> per share on March 31, 2026, resulting in recognized equity consideration of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c4" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ContractualValue" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7904">8.5</ix:nonFraction> million. On April 24, 2026,
the Company paid $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c52" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:PrincipalPlusAccruedInterest" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7905">50</ix:nonFraction> million principal plus accrued interest in cash in satisfaction of its obligations under the senior secured
convertible promissory note.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left; margin: 0pt 0">On September 22, 2025, the Company entered into an agreement with Arjae

In this agreement, the Company is required to make a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c169" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:InstallationPayments" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7906">125,000</ix:nonFraction> per month payment (the &#8220;Installation

the Installation Payments, upon expiration of the installment period, the Company has the option to assign the Commercial &amp; Technical
Proposal dated July 10, 2023, a Purchase Order dated July 1, 2023 and Arjae&#8217;s Terms &amp; Conditions &#8211; Equipment &amp; Material
Supply (the &#8220;Underlying Agreement&#8221;) with respect to the Pecos Slope Helium Recovery Facility. This assignment is subject to
the consent of Arjae, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Should the Company elect not to assign the Underlying Agreement, the
Company may terminate the Underlying Agreement by making a payment to Arjae in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:TerminationPayment" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7907">933,200</ix:nonFraction> (the &#8220;Termination Payment&#8221;).
This payment would be considered the full and final payment relating to the termination of the Underlying Agreement. The Installation
Payments will not be allocated towards the Termination Payment.</p>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="ixv-4359"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 13. FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: left; margin: 0pt 0">The Company accounts for certain liabilities at fair value and classifies
these liabilities with the fair value hierarchy. Our ARO liabilities are measured at fair value on a non-recurring basis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-4630"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>NOTE 14. SEGMENTATION</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">ASC Topic 280, Segment Reporting, establishes standards for companies
to report in their financial statements information about operating segments, products, services, geographic areas, and major customers.
Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise that engage in business activities from which they may recognize revenues
and incur expenses, and for which separate financial information is available that is regularly evaluated by the Company&#8217;s CODM in deciding
how to allocate resources and assess performance.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingCodmProfitLossMeasureHowUsedDescription" id="ixv-4637">The Company&#8217;s CODM has been identified as the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden: hidden-fact-102">Chief Executive Officer</span>,
who reviews total assets and income (loss) from operations of the Company on a consolidated basis to make decisions regarding the allocation
of resources and assessment of financial performance.</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Management evaluated the Company&#8217;s segment reporting conclusion
following the acquisition of the remaining interests in TCDC. Management considered that TCDC represents a significant strategic initiative
of the Company and comprises a substantial portion of the Company&#8217;s consolidated asset base following the acquisition. Management
also considered that executive management devotes significant time to evaluating the development activities, financing arrangements, capital
needs, and strategic direction of TCDC.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">However, management concluded that TCDC did not constitute a separate
operating and reportable segment as of March 31, 2026. Although discrete financial information related to TCDC exists for accounting and
legal entity reporting purposes, the CODM did not regularly review standalone operating results, profitability measures, or other discrete
measures of financial performance for purposes of assessing performance and allocating resources in the manner contemplated by ASC 280.
During the period, TCDC remained in the development stage and had not yet commenced revenue-generating operations. Resource allocation
decisions related to TCDC were made in the context of consolidated liquidity management, financing activities, and enterprise-wide capital
planning rather than through a separate recurring review of operating results or segment profitability.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Accordingly, management determined that the Company operated as a single
operating and reportable segment as of March 31, 2026, as the CODM reviews operating results, allocates resources, and assesses performance
on a consolidated basis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The CODM assesses performance for the single segment and decides how
to allocate resources based on net income or loss as reported in the consolidated statements of operations. The measure of segment assets
and liabilities is reported on the consolidated balance sheets as total assets and total liabilities. <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock" id="ixv-7943">When evaluating the Company's performance
and making key decisions regarding resource allocation, the CODM reviews several key metrics included in net income or loss, total assets,
and total liabilities, which include the following:</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

The total intrinsic value of

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Restricted Stock Awards</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company granted restricted
stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) under the Plan. On January 28, 2026, the Company granted <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c201" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsGranted" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7968">2,442,690</ix:nonFraction> RSUs, and on March 16, 2026, the Company
granted <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c202" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsGranted" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7969">610,673</ix:nonFraction> RSUs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The RSUs entitle the holder to receive <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c203" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisableNumber" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7970">one</ix:nonFraction> share of the Company&#8217;s
common stock for each vested unit. The RSUs generally vest in equal monthly installments over a four-year period, subject to the participant&#8217;s
continued employment with the Company through each applicable vesting date.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The grant-date fair value of the RSUs is based on the closing price
of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the date of grant. Stock-based compensation expense related to RSUs is recognized on a straight-line
basis over the requisite service period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">For the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized stock-based
compensation expense related to RSUs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c204" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7971">781,661</ix:nonFraction>, which is included in general and administrative expenses in the consolidated
statements of operations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">As of March 31, 2026, there was $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c205" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7972">21,373,540</ix:nonFraction> of total unrecognized
stock-based compensation expense related to unvested RSUs, which is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of approximately
<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c206" format="ixt-sec:duryear" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingWeightedAverageRemainingContractualTerm2" id="ixv-7973">3.86</ix:nonNumeric> years.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Performance Awards</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company granted performance
share awards (&#8220;PSUs&#8221;) under the plan. On January 28, 2026, the Company granted an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c207" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsGranted" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7974">7,328,072</ix:nonFraction> PSUs, and on March
16, 2026, the Company granted <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c208" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNonOptionEquityInstrumentsGranted" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-7975">1,221,346</ix:nonFraction> PSUs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The PSUs entitle the holder to receive shares of the Company&#8217;s
common stock upon vesting. The PSUs vest based on the achievement of specified performance and market conditions over a performance period
ending January 1, 2031, subject to certification by the Compensation Committee.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfShareBasedPaymentAwardStockOptionsValuationAssumptionsTableTextBlock" id="ixv-4882"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The grant-date fair value of PSUs with market conditions was determined
using a Monte Carlo simulation model utilizing the following significant assumptions:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The awards include market-based vesting conditions tied to specified
stock price thresholds through January 1, 2031. Stock-based compensation expense related to PSUs is recognized over the requisite service
period based on the grant-date fair value and is not adjusted for actual achievement of market conditions.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Company determined
the performance conditions were probable of achievement and recognized expense accordingly. For the three months ended March 31, 2026,
the Company recognized stock-based compensation expense related to PSUs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c209" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7984">952,441</ix:nonFraction>, which is included in general and administrative
expenses in the consolidated statements of operations.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Term Loan Agreement with Macquarie Equipment Capital Inc.</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 8, 2026, TCDC, entered into a Term Loan Agreement with Macquarie
Equipment Capital Inc. (&#8220;Macquarie&#8221;) for a senior secured term loan facility of up to $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c218" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebtCurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7987">290,000,000</ix:nonFraction> (the &#8220;Term Loan Agreement&#8221;).
The facility consists of a committed $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c219" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebtCurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7988">20,000,000</ix:nonFraction> Term Loan A-1, a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c220" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebtCurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7989">30,000,000</ix:nonFraction> Term Loan A-2, a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c221" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebtCurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7990">40,000,000</ix:nonFraction> Term Loan A-3, and a $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c222" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SecuredDebtCurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7991">200,000,000</ix:nonFraction>
Delayed Draw Term Loan (as defined in the Term Loan Agreement). Borrowings under the Term Loan A-2, Term Loan A-3, and the Delayed Draw
Term Loan are available solely at Macquarie&#8217;s discretion and are subject to certain conditions precedent. TCDC&#8217;s obligations
under the Term Loan Agreement are secured by a first priority perfected security interest in all of the Collateral (as defined in the
Term Loan Agreement), prior to all other liens on the Collateral except for certain permitted liens.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The loans mature on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c223" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="nehc:LoansMaturityDate" id="ixv-7992">April 8, 2029</ix:nonNumeric>, and bear interest at a rate equal
to Term SOFR plus an applicable margin of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c224" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7993">5.50</ix:nonFraction>% for Term Loans A-1 and A-2, and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c225" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-7994">7.75</ix:nonFraction>% for Term Loan A-3 and the Delayed Draw Term Loan.
The borrowings are subject to a multiple on invested capital (MOIC) premium, which is fully earned upon execution of the agreement and
payable upon repayment, prepayment, or acceleration. Depending on the staging of the loans and the timing of the repayment, the required
MOIC ranges from <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c226" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:MultipleOnInvestedCapitalRange" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7995">1.10</ix:nonFraction> to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c227" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:MultipleOnInvestedCapitalRange" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-7996">1.35</ix:nonFraction>. Funding of the Term Loan A-1 was conditioned upon, among other things, the Company closing an underwritten
offering of at least $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c223" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:UnderwrittenOfferingAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7997">50</ix:nonFraction> million. The Term Loan Agreement also includes certain post-closing covenants requiring the Company to establish
an at-the-market program with an aggregate offering price of at least $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c223" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AggregateOfferingPrice" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7998">100</ix:nonFraction> million within 60 days of the closing date and close one or
more sales of equity securities resulting in gross proceeds of at least $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c223" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromDebtNetOfIssuanceCosts" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-7999">30</ix:nonFraction> million within <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c223" format="ixt-sec:durday" name="nehc:NetProceedsClosingDate" id="ixv-8000">60</ix:nonNumeric> days of the closing date. Furthermore, if
a data center lease is not executed within six months of the closing date, or if aggregate loan drawings are less than $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c228" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:FairValueOptionLoansHeldAsAssetsAggregateDifference" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8001">50</ix:nonFraction> million, the
lender may elect to require full prepayment or monthly repayment installments.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Equity Issuances</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">From time to time beginning with the initial funding of the Term Loan
Agreement, the Company may issue certain warrants to purchase common stock (the &#8220;Macquarie Warrants&#8221;) to Macquarie, with an
aggregate value of up to $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c229" decimals="1" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfWarrants" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8002">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million. In connection with the initial funding of the Term Loan Agreement, on April 13, 2026, the Company
issued <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c230" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8003">400,208</ix:nonFraction> Macquarie Warrants to Macquarie, at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c231" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-8004">5.00</ix:nonFraction> and with an aggregate value of approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c230" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfWarrants" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8005">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million.
The Macquarie Warrants are exercisable at any time or from time to time on or before April 8, 2031. The Macquarie Warrants are exercisable
for cash only, subject to customary adjustments. Under the Term Loan Agreement, the Company is required to deliver a Macquarie Warrant
to Macquarie for an aggregate purchase price of up to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c230" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:PercentageOfMarketPrice" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8006">10</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal amount of the applicable Loans (as defined in the Term Loan
Agreement) funded, subject to certain limitations. The Company&#8217;s obligation to issue Macquarie Warrants ceases once the aggregate
outstanding principal amount of the Loans is equal to or greater than $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c232" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:PrincipalAmountOutstandingOnLoansSecuritized" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8007">50,000,000</ix:nonFraction>. The exercise price is equal to the product of (i) <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c231" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:ClassOfWarrantOrRightDeterminationOfNumberOfSharesIssuableNumeratorMultiplicationFactor" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8008">120</ix:nonFraction>%
multiplied by (ii) the five-day volume weighted average price of the Company&#8217;s common stock as of the date of issuance of the Macquarie
Warrants, subject to a minimum price floor of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c233" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:VolumeWeightedAveragePrice" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-8009">4.30</ix:nonFraction>. a price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c235" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SharesIssuedPricePerShare" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-8011">5.00</ix:nonFraction> per share and entered into a Registration Rights Agreement with Macquarie with respect to the resale of these securities.</p></ix:nonNumeric><div>

</div><ix:continuation continuedAt="_SubsequentEventsTextBlock-c0_cont_2" id="_SubsequentEventsTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Shareholder Litigation</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 1, 2026, a federal securities class action lawsuit was filed
in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas against the Company and certain members of its management. The complaint
alleges violations of federal securities laws on behalf of investors who purchased the Company&#8217;s securities between November 6,
2024, and December 29, 2025. The Company intends to vigorously defend itself against these claims.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Underwritten Public Offering of Common Stock</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 9, 2026, New Era Energy &amp; Digital, Inc. announced the
pricing of an underwritten public offering of <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c236" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8012">29,850,746</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at a public offering price of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c237" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:PublicOfferingPrice" scale="0" unitRef="usdPershares" id="ixv-8013">3.35</ix:nonFraction> per share. In
connection with this offering, the Company entered into an underwriting agreement with Northland Securities, Inc., acting as the representative
for the underwriters. Pursuant to this agreement, the Company granted the underwriters a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c238" format="ixt-sec:durday" name="nehc:GrantedTheUnderwritersTerm" id="ixv-8014">30</ix:nonNumeric>-day option to purchase up to an additional
<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c237" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8015">4,477,611</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock at the public offering price, less underwriting discounts. Additionally, the Company agreed to a 90-day
lock-up period during which it may not sell, transfer, or otherwise dispose of any shares of common stock without the prior written consent
of the underwriters, subject to certain exceptions.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 10, 2026, the underwriters exercised their option to purchase
an additional <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c44" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8016">4,477,611</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock (the &#8220;Option Shares&#8221;) at the&#160;public offering&#160;price, less the underwriting
discounts and commissions. The closing of the purchase of the Option Shares by the underwriters occurred on April 14, 2026.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Use of Proceeds and Repayment of Convertible Note</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Company generated approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c44" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceInitialPublicOffering" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8017">93.4</ix:nonFraction> million in net proceeds from
the offering. The primary use of these proceeds was to repay in full all outstanding borrowings under its senior secured convertible promissory
note with SharonAI, Inc., with any remainder to be used for general corporate purposes. This convertible note was originally issued as
part of the acquisition consideration related to the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement dated January 16, 2026, and was repaid in
full on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c239" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" id="ixv-8018">April 24, 2026</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Issuance of Unregistered Equity Securities</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 10, 2026, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c54" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8019">893,724</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common

compensated for the difference in value between shares issued to SharonAI on March 31, 2026, and the shares that would have been received
had the Company&#8217;s recent underwritten public offering closed prior to March 31, 2026. Additionally, on April 10, 2026, the Company
issued <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c240" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ConversionOfStockSharesConverted1" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8020">1,522,389</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock to Zachary Yi Zhou upon the maturity of an Amended and Restated Promissory Note dated April 6,
2026. The maturity of this note was triggered by the closing of the Company&#8217;s underwritten public offering, which qualified as a
Qualified Equity Financing. Both issuances were made pursuant to an exemption from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities
Act of 1933. Following these issuances and the public offering, the Company had <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c241" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8021"><ix:nonFraction contextRef="c241" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" scale="0" unitRef="shares" id="ixv-8022">93,522,797</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock issued and outstanding
as of April 10, 2026.</p></ix:continuation><div>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Convertible Note Prepayment</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 10, 2026, the Company issued written notice to SharonAI, Inc.
of its irrevocable election to prepay its $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c246" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleNotesPayable" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8028">50</ix:nonFraction> million senior secured convertible promissory note in full. Although SharonAI retained the
right to convert up to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c44" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8029">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the note&#8217;s balance into common stock by April 17, 2026, it did not exercise this option. Consequently,
on April 24, 2026, the Company paid the entire $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c52" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DepositLiabilitiesAccruedInterest" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8030">50</ix:nonFraction> million principal balance and all accrued interest in cash. This final payment fully
satisfied the note and concluded all remaining payment obligations related to the Company&#8217;s acquisition of SharonAI, Inc.&#8217;s
equity interests in TCDC.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Executive Employment Agreement and Compensatory Arrangements</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p>

Andrew Casazza to serve as Chief Corporate Officer, effective April 28, 2026. In connection with this appointment, the Company entered
into an employment agreement establishing an annual base salary of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c247" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SalariesAndWages" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-8031">415,000</ix:nonFraction> and an annual target bonus opportunity of up to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c248" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AnnualTargetBonusOpportunityPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8032">40</ix:nonFraction>% of his
base salary, which is contingent upon the achievement of specified performance goals. The employment agreement includes severance provisions
that entitle Mr. Casazza to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c249" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AnnualTargetBonusOpportunityPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8033">100</ix:nonFraction>% of his annual base salary, along with earned and pro-rated bonuses and a lump sum payment for 12 months
of benefit premiums, in the event he is terminated without Cause or resigns for Good Reason (as defined in the employment agreement) prior
to a Change in Control (as defined in the employment agreement). If such a qualifying termination occurs on or after a Change in Control,
the severance compensation increases to <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c250" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nehc:AnnualTargetBonusOpportunityPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-8034">150</ix:nonFraction>% of his base salary and 18 months of benefit premium payments.</p>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><i>The following
discussion and analysis summarizes the significant factors affecting our operating results, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows
as of and for the periods presented below. The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our financial statements
and the related notes thereto included elsewhere in this Report. The discussion contains forward-looking statements that are based on
the beliefs of management, as well as assumptions made by, and information currently available to, management. Actual results could differ
materially from those discussed in or implied by forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those discussed
below and elsewhere in this Report, particularly in the sections titled &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; and &#8220;Cautionary Note Regarding
Forward-Looking Statements.&#8221;</i></span></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><i>&#160;</i></span></p><div>

Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; to &#8220;New Era,&#8221; &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221;,
&#8220;our&#8221;, and the &#8220;Company&#8221; are intended to refer to (i) following the Business Combination (as defined below), the
business and operations of New Era Energy &amp; Digital, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, and (ii) prior to the Business Combination,
New Era Energy &amp; Digital, Inc. (the predecessor entity in existence prior to the consummation of the Business Combination) and its
consolidated subsidiary.</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Business Overview and Strategy</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>&#160;</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">New Era Energy &amp; Digital, Inc. was initially incorporated in the
State of Delaware on November 5, 2020 under the name Roth CH Acquisition V Co., which was formed for the purpose of entering into a merger,
share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, recapitalization, reorganization or other similar business combination with one or
more target businesses. Roth CH Acquisition V Co. consummated an initial public offering, after which its securities began trading on
the Nasdaq on December 1, 2021. In December 2024, Roth CH Acquisition V Co. merged with and into Roth CH V Holdings, Inc., a Nevada corporation
and a wholly owned subsidiary of Roth CH Acquisition V Co., formed on June 24, 2024, for the sole purpose of reincorporating Roth CH Acquisition
V Co. into the State of Nevada, with Roth CH V Holdings, Inc. surviving such merger.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">Immediately following the reincorporation, the Company completed its
business combination (the &#8220;Business Combination&#8221;) with New Era Helium Corp., a Nevada corporation, pursuant to that certain
Business Combination Agreement and Plan of Reorganization, dated as of January 3, 2024 (as amended on June 5, 2024, August 8, 2024, September
11, 2024, and September 30, 2024, the &#8220;BCA&#8221;), by and among New Era Helium Corp., Roth CH Acquisition V Co., Roth CH V Holdings,
Inc., and Roth CH V Merger Sub Corp., a Delaware corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Roth CH Acquisition V Co. The Company subsequently
changed its name to &#8220;New Era Helium, Inc.&#8221; and later to &#8220;New Era Energy &amp; Digital, Inc.&#8221;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">We are a vertically-integrated developer and operator of next-generation
digital infrastructure and integrated power assets accelerating speed-to-power for advanced AI hyperscalers. In the second half of 2025,
we executed a strategic pivot from our legacy natural gas operations to focus exclusively on developing data center campuses where power,
land, and connectivity can be assembled and delivered on accelerated timelines. Our mission is to deliver speed-to-power by converging
behind-the-meter power flexibility with data center development capabilities. Our primary strategy is to aggregate and entitle &#8220;Powered
Land&#8221; and to develop &#8220;Powered Shells&#8221; and build-to-suit assets in power-advantaged markets, beginning with the Permian
Basin, which benefits from energy abundance, regulatory clarity, and fiber connectivity.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

</div><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 33; Value: 1 --><div>
    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->30<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
    </div><div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 12pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></div><div>
    </div><!-- Field: /Page --><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">We are initially focused on our flagship project, TCDC, a 438-acre
campus in Ector County, Texas, designed to support over 1 GW of potential compute capacity through phased development, with projected
power delivery beginning as early as the end of 2027. We believe our proximity to major natural gas pipelines, fiber networks and CO2
pipelines will provide us with the ability to serve our customers lower transmission costs and best-in-class uptime for purposes of reliably
generating AI compute to capitalize on the AI revolution. We intend to execute through partnering across engineering, construction, procurement,
power generation and sustainability with a world-class developer partner to provide our hyperscaler tenants with certainty of execution
and speed-to-power.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b>Recent Developments</b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Term Loan Agreement with Macquarie Equipment Capital Inc.</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On April 8, 2026, TCDC, entered into a Term Loan Agreement with Macquarie
Equipment Capital Inc. (&#8220;Macquarie&#8221;) for a senior secured term loan facility of up to $290,000,000 (the &#8220;Term Loan Agreement&#8221;).
The facility consists of a committed $20,000,000 Term Loan A-1, a $30,000,000 Term Loan A-2, a $40,000,000 Term Loan A-3, and a $200,000,000
Delayed Draw Term Loan (as defined in the Term Loan Agreement). Borrowings under the Term Loan A-2, Term Loan A-3, and the Delayed Draw
Term Loan are available solely at Macquarie&#8217;s discretion and are subject to certain conditions precedent. TCDC&#8217;s obligations
under the Term Loan Agreement are secured by a first priority perfected security interest in all of the Collateral (as defined in the
Term Loan Agreement), prior to all other liens on the Collateral except for certain permitted liens.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The loans mature on April 8, 2029, and bear interest at a rate equal
to Term SOFR plus an applicable margin of 5.50% for Term Loans A-1 and A-2, and 7.75% for Term Loan A-3 and the Delayed Draw Term Loan.
The borrowings are subject to a multiple on invested capital (&#8220;MOIC&#8221;) premium, which is fully earned upon execution of the
agreement and payable upon repayment, prepayment, or acceleration. Depending on the staging of the loans and the timing of the repayment,
the required MOIC ranges from 1.10 to 1.35. Funding of the Term Loan A-1 was conditioned upon, among other things, the Company closing
an underwritten offering of at least $50 million. The Term Loan Agreement also includes certain post-closing covenants requiring the Company
to establish an at-the-market program with an aggregate offering price of at least $100 million within 60 days of the closing date and
close one or more sales of equity securities resulting in gross proceeds of at least $30 million within 60 days of the closing date. Furthermore,
if a data center lease is not executed within six months of the closing date, or if aggregate loan drawings are less than $50 million,
the lender may elect to require full prepayment or monthly repayment installments.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>SharonAI Purchase Agreement</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On January 21, 2025, we entered into a Limited Liability Company Agreement
(the &#8220;LLC Agreement&#8221;) with SharonAI for the creation of TCDC as a joint venture of the Company and SharonAI (the &#8220;Joint
Venture&#8221;). Pursuant to the terms of the LLC Agreement, the purpose of the Joint Venture was to engage in (i) the purchase, building,
and development of a site in Texas with an initial 250 MW gas-fired power plant and corresponding data center, (ii) the operation of this
site, and (iii) any and all lawful activities necessary or incidental thereto.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">The Company made a $75,000 contribution to the Joint Venture on April
16, 2025. On July 16, 2025, the Company made an additional contribution of $750,000. On September 26, 2025, the Company made an additional
contribution of $25,000. On November 21, 2025, the Company made an additional contribution of $12,500.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>Senior Secured Convertible Promissory Note</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><i>&#160;</i></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On January 16, 2026, we acquired the remaining 50% member interest
in TCDC, from SharonAI, pursuant to the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;SharonAI Purchase Agreement&#8221;), dated
as of January 16, 2026, by and between the Company and SharonAI, for an aggregate purchase price of $70 million, of which (a) $10 million
is payable in cash, (b) $10 million is payable in equity securities to be issued in connection with the Company&#8217;s next equity financing
transaction, and (c) $50 million is payable in the form of a senior secured convertible promissory note (the &#8220;Convertible Note&#8221;).
The entirety of the acquisition consideration is subject to a 19.99% ownership cap. On March 31, 2026, the Company paid SharonAI $9.85
million in cash and issued to SharonAI 2,091,351 shares of common stock (at a price per share of $4.78) in satisfaction of the Company&#8217;s
obligation to pay $10 million in equity securities under the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement.&#160;On April 24, 2026, the Company
paid $50 million principal plus accrued interest in cash in satisfaction of its obligations under the Convertible Note.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>Investor Waiver</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">On February 1, 2026, the Company entered into an Amended and Restated
Consent and Waiver (the &#8220;Amended Waiver&#8221;) with ATW AI Infrastructure II LLC (the &#8220;Investor&#8221;) pursuant to which
the Investor agreed to partially waive the anti-dilution provisions of the First Tranche Warrant and Second Tranche Warrant (the &#8220;Investor
Warrants&#8221;) such that the exercise prices of the First Tranche Warrant and Second Tranche Warrant were each adjusted down solely
to $2.00. As a result of the anti-dilution adjustments in the Investor Warrants, as modified by the Amended Waiver, the number of shares
of common stock of the Company issuable pursuant to the First Tranche Warrant total 5.5 million shares and the number of shares of common
stock issuable pursuant to the Second Tranche Warrant total 10.7 million shares.</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&#160;</p><div>

</div><p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"></p><div>

    </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1.5pt solid"><p style="font: normal 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->31<!-- Field: /Sequence --></p></div><div>
